jamb/english.name: Use of English
jamb/english.title: JAMB Use of English practice questions 2027 (free CBT) | CrackIt
jamb/english.h1: JAMB Use of English practice: free CBT questions with answers
jamb/english.intro: Use of English is the one subject every UTME candidate writes, and it carries the most questions on the paper. It tests vocabulary (synonyms, antonyms, sentence completion), grammar (concord, tenses, prepositions, question tags), idioms, sentence interpretation and Oral English (vowels, consonants, stress and rhymes).
tips: Oral English questions are quick marks once you know the sound groups. Practise vowel and consonant sounds and word stress a little every day instead of cramming them.
For synonyms and antonyms, read the whole sentence first: the right option fits the meaning in that sentence, not only the dictionary meaning.
Concord and tense questions follow a small set of rules (collective nouns, "neither … nor", "one of the …"). Learn the rule from each wrong answer, not just the answer.

jamb/mathematics.name: Mathematics
jamb/mathematics.title: JAMB Mathematics practice questions 2027 with solutions | CrackIt
jamb/mathematics.h1: JAMB Mathematics practice: free CBT questions with worked answers
jamb/mathematics.intro: UTME Mathematics covers number and numeration (number bases, indices, logarithms, surds), algebra (equations, variation, progressions, matrices), geometry and trigonometry, calculus (differentiation and integration) and statistics and probability. Speed matters: you have about the same time per question as in other subjects, but many need working.
tips: Learn the short methods for number bases, indices and logarithms. They appear often and can be done in under a minute each.
Use the on-screen calculator in the CBT practice the way you will in the real exam, so you are not slowed down on the day.
If a question takes more than two minutes, flag it, move on and come back. Every question carries the same mark.

jamb/physics.name: Physics
jamb/physics.title: JAMB Physics practice questions 2027 with explanations | CrackIt
jamb/physics.h1: JAMB Physics practice: free CBT questions with explanations
jamb/physics.intro: UTME Physics moves from measurement and motion (vectors, equations of motion, projectiles, Newton's laws) through energy, heat and gas laws, waves, sound and light, to electricity, magnetism and modern physics (radioactivity, half-life, photoelectric effect). Most questions need one formula used correctly with the right units.
tips: Write the formula and the units before you calculate. Many wrong options are what you get from a units slip (cm instead of m, minutes instead of seconds).
Resistors in series and parallel, lenses and half-life come up again and again. Practise them until they are automatic.
For theory questions on waves, light and modern physics, read all four options: two are often nearly right.

jamb/chemistry.name: Chemistry
jamb/chemistry.title: JAMB Chemistry practice questions 2027 with answers | CrackIt
jamb/chemistry.h1: JAMB Chemistry practice: free CBT questions with answers
jamb/chemistry.intro: UTME Chemistry covers separation techniques, gas laws and kinetic theory, atomic structure and the periodic table, bonding, the mole concept and stoichiometry, acids, bases and salts, redox and electrolysis, energy, rates and equilibrium, metals and non-metals, organic chemistry and Nigeria's petroleum industry.
tips: The mole concept sits behind many calculation questions. Get comfortable converting between mass, moles, volume of gas and number of particles.
Electrolysis and Faraday's laws, and Le Chatelier's principle, are favourite topics. Practise both the calculations and the reasoning.
For organic chemistry, learn the functional groups and their typical reactions as a table you can picture.

jamb/biology.name: Biology
jamb/biology.title: JAMB Biology practice questions 2027 with explanations | CrackIt
jamb/biology.h1: JAMB Biology practice: free CBT questions with explanations
jamb/biology.intro: UTME Biology spans the variety of living things and classification, cells and their properties, nutrition, transport, respiration and excretion, support and reproduction, coordination and hormones, ecology (including Nigerian biomes), genetics and heredity, evolution, and disease and immunity.
tips: Genetics crosses (ratios, blood groups, sex-linked traits) are reliable marks. Draw the Punnett square every time, even when it looks easy.
Ecology and conservation questions often use Nigerian examples. Know the vegetation zones and their typical plants and animals.
Make a one-page table of organs and their functions for each body system. Many questions test exactly that link.

jamb/economics.name: Economics
jamb/economics.title: JAMB Economics practice questions 2027 with answers | CrackIt
jamb/economics.h1: JAMB Economics practice: free CBT questions with answers
jamb/economics.intro: UTME Economics tests basic concepts (scarcity, choice, opportunity cost), demand, supply, price and elasticity, production and costs, market structures, national income, money and inflation, Nigerian financial institutions, public finance, development, agriculture and industry in Nigeria, population, international trade and the labour market.
tips: Demand and supply graphs are the heart of the paper. Practise telling a shift of the curve from a movement along it.
Learn the cost formulas (average, marginal, fixed and variable) and the national income measures (GDP, GNP, NNP) side by side.
Read the Nigerian sections closely: the Central Bank, petroleum and agriculture questions reward up-to-date basics.

jamb/government.name: Government
jamb/government.title: JAMB Government practice questions 2027 with answers | CrackIt
jamb/government.h1: JAMB Government practice: free CBT questions with answers
jamb/government.intro: UTME Government covers political concepts (power, authority, sovereignty, democracy), forms and organs of government, constitutions and the rule of law, parties, pressure groups and elections, the civil service, pre-colonial and colonial Nigeria, nationalism, constitutional development and federalism, military rule, local government, foreign policy and international organisations.
tips: Nigeria's constitutional history is a timeline. Learn each constitution with its year and one feature it introduced.
Many questions turn on one key word (sovereignty, legitimacy, delegated legislation). Know the precise definitions.
International organisations (UN, AU, ECOWAS, Commonwealth, OPEC): learn when each was founded, its headquarters and one main aim.

waec/english.name: English Language
waec/english.title: WAEC English Language objective practice 2027 (free CBT) | CrackIt
waec/english.h1: WAEC English Language objectives: free practice with answers
waec/english.intro: The objective paper of WASSCE English Language tests lexis and structure: synonyms and antonyms, sentence completion, concord, tenses, prepositions, idioms, sentence interpretation, register, and Oral English (vowels, consonants, stress and rhymes). CrackIt practises this objective part on a CBT screen with grades from A1 to F9.
tips: Never leave a question blank: there is no negative marking on the objective paper.
Register questions (the vocabulary of fields like banking, medicine or law) come up every year. Learn a few words from each field.
Mark your Oral English weak spots in practice and repeat only those. It is the fastest way to add marks.

waec/mathematics.name: General Mathematics
waec/mathematics.title: WAEC General Mathematics objective practice 2027 | CrackIt
waec/mathematics.h1: WAEC General Mathematics objectives: free practice with solutions
waec/mathematics.intro: WASSCE General Mathematics objectives cover number and numeration, algebra, mensuration, geometry and trigonometry, statistics and probability. CrackIt sets you a timed CBT-style objective paper, grades it A1 to F9 and shows a worked explanation for every question.
tips: Most university courses ask for a credit (C6 or better) in Mathematics. Track your grade in CrackIt and see how far you are from C6.
Mensuration and statistics questions often reuse the same formulas. Write them on one card and practise with them every week.
Time yourself: the objective paper is long, so aim for about one minute per question and come back to the hard ones.

waec/biology.name: Biology
waec/biology.title: WAEC Biology objective practice 2027 with explanations | CrackIt
waec/biology.h1: WAEC Biology objectives: free practice with explanations
waec/biology.intro: WASSCE Biology objectives test the cell, classification, nutrition, transport, respiration, excretion, reproduction, coordination, ecology, genetics and evolution, with many questions based on Nigerian and West African examples. CrackIt practises the objective paper with grades A1 to F9.
tips: Use the 5-credits tracker: Biology is a core science credit for medicine, nursing, pharmacy and agriculture courses.
Ecology questions often describe a habitat. Practise naming the ecological factor or relationship being described.
Practise reading diagrams in words: many objective questions describe a structure and ask for its function.

Below are the facts we could verify from published sources, and 5 free original practice questions in the style of the screening (English, Mathematics and General knowledge).
tips: Your UTME score counts for the biggest share of the UNILAG aggregate, but the Post-UTME can still move you above or below the departmental cut-off. Treat it seriously.
Use the free Admission Chance Checker to see what Post-UTME score you need for your course.

post-utme/oau.intro: Obafemi Awolowo University (OAU), Ile-Ife screens candidates and combines the result with your UTME score and O'level grades into an aggregate. Below are the facts we could verify from published sources, and 5 free original practice questions in the style of the screening.
tips: At OAU the Post-UTME carries a large share of the aggregate (see the formula below), so preparation pays off directly.
Check your O'level grades: they add points to your aggregate, so a B3 instead of a C6 matters.
